title: Intermittent rapamycin feeding recapitulates some effects of continuous treatment while maintaining lifespan extension - ScienceDirect
abstract:
Intermittent rapamycin treatment extends lifespan to the same extent as chronic feeding in male but not female mice. ... Intermittent rapamycin feeding increases metabolic health compared to chronic feeding.
Intermittent rapamycin treatment extends lifespan to the same extent as chronic feeding in male but not female mice. ... Intermittent rapamycin feeding increases metabolic health compared to chronic feeding. ... Chronic rapamycin treatment is more efficient in reducing tumour growth and age-related inflammation.
Organ specific pathology was assessed at 24 months of age. Chronic rapamycin treatment induced glucose intolerance, which was partially ameliorated by intermittent treatment. Chronic and intermittent rapamycin treatments increased lifespan equally in males, while in females chronic treatment resulted in slightly higher survival.
However, other health parameters, including age related pathologies, were better prevented by continuous treatment. Intermittent rapamycin treatment is effective in prolonging lifespan and reduces some side-effects of chronic treatment, but chronic treatment is more beneficial to healthspan.
Rapamycin, a powerful geroprotective drug, can have detrimental effects when administered chronically. We determined whether intermittent treatment of mice can reduce negative effects while maintaining benefits of chronic treatment. From 6 months of age, male and female C3B6F1 hybrid mice were either continuously fed with 42 mg/kg rapamycin, or intermittently fed by alternating weekly feeding of 42 mg/kg rapamycin food with weekly control feeding.
